Source way order and shared node IDs are retained. No nearby endpoints are joined and no reference boundaries are read.

Produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union, EU-DEM layers.

sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 61 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. There is no saved GPS start gate; the simulation begins at the first trace coordinate. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Sparse source-ordered road-edge estimates read independently on the pinned IGN BD ORTHO image, requested at approximately 0.20 m ground pixels. Pixel transects help locate pavement or painted-edge transitions; their signal scores are not positional confidence. The original mapped route is retained. Control coordinates and nominal raster spacing do not establish survey accuracy. A visible section at original source station15 starts the measurement grid. Unmeasured gantry, side-path, branch and apron joins interpolate between observed ends, including35-45,180-190,305-315 and505-2. Shadowed left sections210-230,230-250 and250-254 and the shadowed right430-450 and470-490 stretches also interpolate. Road limits through shared paving are estimates of the driving corridor, not every connected apron. Capture date is unconfirmed; retrieval time is not capture time. Direction and named configuration remain draft, timing is missing, curbs illustrative and banking unknown.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed directly from complete, sparse image measurements on the existing trace cross-sections. All intervals interpolate between image anchors; they are not automatic detections or a continuous edge survey. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. Isolated missing pixels inside the road are not filled or used as boundary evidence. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. These borders have not been formally verified.
